title: Work on ints with the primitive specializations

blocks.text: For primitive values, `java.util.function` has specializations that skip boxing each `int` into an `Integer`: `IntPredicate` instead of `Predicate<Integer>`, `IntFunction<R>` instead of `Function<Integer, R>`, `ToIntFunction<T>` instead of `Function<T, Integer>`, and `IntBinaryOperator` instead of `BinaryOperator<Integer>`.
Write four static methods of `PrimitiveOps`, each built on the specialization named:

items: `int[] odds(int[] numbers)` keeps the odd numbers, in order (`IntPredicate`).
`List<String> padded(int[] numbers)` writes each number with at least five digits, zero-padded (`IntFunction<String>`).
`int totalLength(List<String> texts)` sums the lengths of the strings (`ToIntFunction<String>`).
`int product(int[] numbers)` multiplies the numbers together (`IntBinaryOperator`).

blocks.text: Remember that numbers can be negative, and that an array can be empty.

cases.says: It keeps odd numbers, pads to five digits, sums lengths and multiplies.
A negative odd number leaves remainder -1, not 1, and is still odd.
The product of no numbers is 1, the identity of multiplication.

concepts: IntPredicate, IntFunction, ToIntFunction and IntBinaryOperator work on int values directly.
